json.reason: The bug class is using the result of getAccount() — which returns null for closed or missing accounts — without a null guard before dereferencing it. That is a project-specific nullable-return contract detectable from syntax.
json.title: getAccount() result used without null check
json.message: getAccount() can return null (closed or missing account); $V is never null-checked before use.
json.note: getAccount() returns null when the account does not exist or is closed, so dereferencing the result (e.g. $V.balance) throws a TypeError at runtime. Guard the value right after the call, e.g. `if (!$V) throw new Error("account not found or closed");`, or access it with optional chaining.
json.rule_yaml:
rule:
  kind: lexical_declaration
  any:
    - pattern: const $V = getAccount($$$A)
    - pattern: let $V = getAccount($$$A)
  not:
    inside:
      kind: statement_block
      stopBy: end
      has:
        stopBy: end
        any:
          - pattern: "!$V"
          - pattern: $V == null
          - pattern: $V === null
          - pattern: $V != null
          - pattern: $V !== null
          - pattern: $V === undefined
          - pattern: $V !== undefined
          - pattern: $V?.$F
          - pattern: "if ($V) { $$$BODY }"
          - pattern: $V && $RHS
          - pattern: $V ?? $ALT
